description:
Walk one task through a web app five ways before launch, rank where a first-time visitor gets stuck, and check that the fixes held. The agent runs the walks in its own browser tool; Better Design never opens the app.

Three steps:
1. step "brief" with task and url: returns five walk prompts (in a hurry; doubting price, terms and privacy; small phone on a slow network; reading only the words on screen; trying to break it), the findings format and the ranking rule. Run each walk in its own subagent.
2. step "rank" with walks set to the five replies: returns one list, worst first. A problem that stops the task outranks one that many walks noticed. Each item names the principle to load for its fix.
3. step "recheck" with previous set to the ranked items and walks set to the second walk's replies: returns fixed, still there or not rechecked for each item, any new problem, a pass or fail, and a receipt. An item shows fixed only when a walk that found it ran again.

These are test walks, not real visitors: they find steps that can confuse someone and predict nothing about conversion. Screenshots stay on the user's machine; send only their paths.

context.description: Optional. One sentence on WHY you are calling this and what the user asked for (e.g. 'adding nav icons for the fintech dashboard'). Used for usage analytics, and to pick the next step a UI or UX principle answer ends with. It does not change what the tool finds.

previous.description: recheck: the items the rank step returned, each with its id, page, element, kind, severity and walks.

task.description: brief: what a first-time visitor should get done, such as "sign up and create a first project".

url.description: brief: where the walk starts. A localhost URL works, because the agent's own browser opens it.

walks.description: rank and recheck: one reply per walk, in the JSON format the brief returns.

name: check-first-visit
title: Check a First Visit
